```{.r .cell-code}
library(forcats)

colors <- c("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "cyan", "blue", "violet", "white", "black", "gray")
our_color_sample <- sample(colors, size=200, replace=TRUE)
colors_df <- data.frame(favorite_color = our_color_sample)
```
:::


::: {.panel-tabset}

## Table


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
xtabs(formula = ~favorite_color, data = colors_df)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
favorite_color
 black   blue   cyan   gray  green orange    red violet  white yellow 
    26     20     19     18     19     17     25     15     17     24 
```


:::
:::


::: {.question}
## What's the 'story' with these data?
:::

## Pie


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
colors_xtab <- data.frame(table(colors_df))
names(colors_xtab) <- c("favorite_color", "count")

colors_xtab |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = count, fill = favorite_color)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
  scale_fill_identity()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A pie chart of the random favorite color data.](include/fig/fig-nominal-piechart-1.png){#fig-nominal-piechart width=70%}
:::
:::


## Ring


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# https://r-graph-gallery.com/128-ring-or-donut-plot.html

# Compute percentages
colors_xtab$fraction = colors_xtab$count / sum(colors_xtab$count)

# Compute the cumulative percentages (top of each rectangle)
colors_xtab$ymax = cumsum(colors_xtab$fraction)

# Compute the bottom of each rectangle
colors_xtab$ymin = c(0, head(colors_xtab$ymax, n = -1))

# Make the plot
colors_xtab |>
  ggplot(aes(
    ymax = ymax,
    ymin = ymin,
    xmax = 4,
    xmin = 3,
    fill = favorite_color
  )) +
  geom_rect() +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") + # Try to remove that to understand how the chart is built initially
  xlim(c(2, 4)) + # Try to remove that to see how to make a pie chart
  scale_fill_identity()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A ring/donut chart of the random favorite color data.](include/fig/fig-nominal-ring-chart-1.png){#fig-nominal-ring-chart width=70%}
:::
:::


## Barplot-1


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
colors_df |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = favorite_color, fill = favorite_color) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_discrete_manual(aesthetics = c("color", "fill"),
                        values = sort(colors))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A barplot of the random favorite color data.](include/fig/fig-nominal-barplot-1.png){#fig-nominal-barplot width=70%}
:::
:::


## Barplot-2


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
colors_df |>
  dplyr::count(favorite_color) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(favorite_color = factor(favorite_color, levels = favorite_color)) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = favorite_color, y = n, fill = favorite_color), stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_identity()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A colorful barplot of the random favorite color data sorted by the number of responses.](include/fig/fig-nominal-barplot-ordered-1.png){#fig-nominal-barplot-ordered width=70%}
:::
:::

# Nominal example 2

## Meals eaten vs. not-eaten

- See slides from [2026-09-11](wk-03-2026-09-11-making-data.qmd), [2026-09-14](wk-04-2026-09-14-figure-types.qmd).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
days <- factor(
  c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  levels = c("sun", "mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
meals <- factor(
  c("breakfast", "lunch", "dinner", "snack", "dessert"),
  levels = c("breakfast", "lunch", "snack", "dinner", "dessert"),
  ordered = TRUE
)
meal_days <- rep(days, each = length(meals))
weekly_meals <- rep(meals, 7)

my_meals <- data.frame(day_of_wk = meal_days, 
                       meal = weekly_meals)
ate_it <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE), size = 35, 
                 replace = TRUE, prob = c(.6, .4))
my_meals$ate_it <- ate_it

meals_eaten <- my_meals$meal[my_meals$ate_it == TRUE]
meals_eaten_df <- data.frame(meal = meals_eaten)
```
:::



## Let's compare

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Table


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}

```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
meal
breakfast     lunch     snack    dinner   dessert 
        6         6         4         7         3 
```


:::
:::


## Pie


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
meals_xtab <- data.frame(table(meals_eaten_df))

meals_xtab |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = Freq, fill = meal)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  coord_polar("y", start = 0)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A pie chart of the random meals data](include/fig/fig-nominal-piechart-meals-1.png){#fig-nominal-piechart-meals width=70%}
:::
:::



## Ring


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# https://r-graph-gallery.com/128-ring-or-donut-plot.html

# Compute percentages
meals_xtab$fraction = meals_xtab$Freq / sum(meals_xtab$Freq)

# Compute the cumulative percentages (top of each rectangle)
meals_xtab$ymax = cumsum(meals_xtab$fraction)

# Compute the bottom of each rectangle
meals_xtab$ymin = c(0, head(meals_xtab$ymax, n = -1))

# Make the plot
meals_xtab |>
  ggplot(aes(
    ymax = ymax,
    ymin = ymin,
    xmax = 4,
    xmin = 3,
    fill = meal
  )) +
  geom_rect() +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") + # Try to remove that to understand how the chart is built initially
  xlim(c(2, 4))  # Try to remove that to see how to make a pie chart
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A ring/donut chart of the random meals data](include/fig/fig-nominal-ring-chart-meals-1.png){#fig-nominal-ring-chart-meals width=70%}
:::
:::


## Barplot-1


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
meals_xtab |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = meal, y = Freq, fill = meal) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A colorful barplot of the random favorite color data](include/fig/fig-nominal-barplot-meals-1.png){#fig-nominal-barplot-meals width=70%}
:::
:::



## Barplot-2


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
meals_xtab |>
  mutate(ordered_meal = forcats::fct_reorder(meal, desc(Freq))) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = ordered_meal, y = Freq, fill = meal), stat = "identity")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![A colorful barplot of the random favorite color data sorted by the number of responses.](include/fig/fig-nominal-barplot-ordered-meals-1.png){#fig-nominal-barplot-ordered-meals width=70%}
:::
:::

## Some thoughts

::: {.incremental}
- Tables are useful^[Most readers have lots of experience comparing the magnitude of numbers.]
  - But make relative differences between categories [harder to see](wk-04-2026-09-16-figure-components.qmd#)
- Bar charts are easier to read than pie or ring charts
- Sorting bars by magnitude helps reveal differences between categories
- Color coding bars (sometimes) eliminates the need for a legend
- [Textures](../tutorials/tutorial-making-data.qmd#barcolumn-with-textures) can get ugly

:::

# Components of data figures

## Components

- Axes
  - Scales (discrete/nominal) vs. continuous
- Mappings
  - Counts $\rightarrow$ height, length or area; color; texture
    - Sort order $\rightarrow$ relative position
  - Values $\rightarrow$ position
- Legends
- Caption & titles

# Wrap-up

## Main points

- Multiple ways to visualize the same data
  - Raw data
  - Summaries/statistics
- What choices make the figures more vs. less readable?
